title: A layout cursor
description:
Implement the layout model behind ImGui-style windows. A `Layout` places widgets inside a content area that starts at `(left, top)` and is `width` wide.

- Each `item(w, h)` places a widget of that size and returns its top-left position.
- Normally an item goes at the start of a new line: x at `left`, y below the previous line. A line's height is the tallest item on it; the next line starts `spacingY` below that.
- `sameLine()` makes the **next** item continue on the current line, `spacingX` to the right of the previous item.
- `sameLineAt(x)` makes the next item continue on the current line at `left + x`.
- `indent(d)` moves `left` (for new lines) by `d`; negative values unindent.
- An item with `w` of `-1` fills the remaining width of the line: from its x to `left + width` (where `left` is the content area's original left edge plus any indent). Return its size too.

Return `Placed{ x, y, w, h }` for each item.

```
Layout l{ 10, 20, 300, 8, 4 };     // left, top, width, spacingX, spacingY
item(100, 20)   -> (10, 20)
item(50, 30)    -> (10, 44)        // new line: 20 + 20 + 4
sameLine(); item(60, 10) -> (68, 44)
item(-1, 16)    -> (10, 78, 300, 16)   // new line below the 30-high line; fills the width
```
hints: Keep the y of the current line, its height so far, and the x where the next item on the same line would go. A new line starts `lineHeight + spacingY` below the current line's y.
`sameLine` only sets a flag for the next item; `item` clears it after placing.
For a fill item (`w == -1`), the width is the distance from its x to the content area's right edge, which never moves when indenting.
